statement: Frontier 50%-success task time horizon >= 16 h (METR measurements, cross-checked against government AISI reports; by 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: The 50%-time-horizon metric did not exist in 2023 (METR introduced it in 2025). The closest in-phase evidence was the evaluator's (then ARC Evals) Dec 2023 report: agents built on contemporary frontier models completed only the easiest of 12 autonomy tasks. No government AISI had yet published agent-autonomy measurements.

items.summary: No task-time-horizon measurement series existed during 2023; the indicator's metric was introduced later.
items.detail: METR time-horizon methodology first published March 2025 (outside phase). In-phase proxy recorded below.

items.summary: Independent evaluator report: four example language-model agents were tested on 12 tasks relevant to autonomous replication and adaptation; they completed only the easiest tasks, with partial progress on harder ones. The authors warn the evaluations cannot rule out such capability in the next model generation (~100x effective compute).
items.detail: Kinniment et al. (METR, then ARC Evals), 'Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks', arXiv:2312.11671 v1 2023-12-18 (verified via web_extract this run). Implies frontier autonomous task horizons far below 16 h at end-2023.
